title: The Last Static
premise: Ulyana Thornbury tends the Verdance, a terraforming garden on the fringe moon of Callow's Rest, and keeps lit a beacon whose original purpose was lost with the generation that built it. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with its crew aged backward into children, Ulyana discovers the beacon is a countdown lock — a lie of maintenance records he must sustain to keep two rival fleets from jumping into the same window and annihilating each other over the children. As the truth about the beacon's commissioning surfaces, Ulyana must choose between the loyalty his inherited role demands and the truth that could save the children, ultimately broadcasting the real signal and letting the fleets collide with the truth instead of each other, ending with the garden opened to a generation that finally has someone born to receive it.
about_author: Beatrix Zhou is the pen name of a former hydrology consultant who spent a decade writing technical reports about water nobody would drink for fifty years. She now writes science fiction about people who maintain things for futures they will never see, and lives with her partner and an unreasonable number of ferns.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Hours
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet him mid-rotation in the Verdance, calibrating moisture lines and logging the beacon's routine pulse as he has every day since inheriting the post from a mentor who never explained it. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness disguised as devotion — a man who has made peace with tending for the unborn.

chapters.title: A Light Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine query from the Colonial Authority asks who commissioned the beacon; Ulyana fabricates an answer using his mentor's old templates, the first lie told in the beacon's name. The beat is unease — the comfort of routine cracking under a single question he cannot answer honestly.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, shifting to the Meridian's child-crew member Sef in the final third. The Meridian decants from jump space wrong: forty crew, all aged backward to under ten years old, transmitting a distress call in adult voices recorded years ago. The beat is dread and wonder colliding as Ulyana realizes the beacon heard them coming.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, fragmented and childlike but retaining adult memory shards. The children wake on the Meridian with no idea what happened to them, finding their own aged belongings. The beat is uncanny grief — Sef remembers being forty and cannot reconcile it with hands that won't stop growing.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Corporate Combine fleet arrives claiming salvage jurisdiction over the Meridian; the Founders' Compact fleet follows claiming custody of its citizens. Ulyana, as the only neutral party with a licensed station, is legally obliged to harbor the children. The beat is the terrible weight of accidental significance.

chapters.title: The Verdance Fills
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Sef POVs. Twenty-two children are quartered in the garden habitat; Sef, oldest at nine, appoints himself their spokesperson. Ulyana teaches them to tend seedlings, and the garden — built for the unborn — finally holds living children. The beat is tentative found-family warmth shadowed by the fleets massing in orbit.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Window
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV with intercepted fleet communications. Both fleets discover the jump window — the only route home — closes in nineteen days, and both calculate they need the Meridian's intact drive core to make it. The beat is escalating stakes as diplomacy curdles into positioning.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Deep in the beacon's maintenance strata, Ulyana finds his mentor's sealed logs: the beacon is a jump-window arbitration lock, designed to certify one fleet's priority — and the mentor falsified its certification decades ago to favor the Founders. The beat is betrayal; the inheritance is a lie.

chapters.title: Sef Remembers the Bridge
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Fragmented adult memories surface: Sef was the Meridian's navigator and knew about the beacon's true function, knew the crew was aged backward deliberately — an experiment in surviving long jumps. The beat is horror refracted through a child's voice as the pieces align.

chapters.title: The Combine's Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Combine Admiral Voss offers Ulyana protection and a future for the children if he recertifies the beacon in the Combine's favor — exploiting the same falsification mechanism his mentor used. The beat is temptation with a clean conscience attached, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Inherited
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, a quiet chapter. Ulyana reads his mentor's letters and understands the falsification was an act of loyalty to people long dead, maintained out of love. He must decide whether inherited loyalty binds him. The beat is the theme made intimate: what do we owe the dead who shaped us?

chapters.title: Small Mutinies
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The children, coached by fragments of Sef's navigator memory, sabotage a Combine boarding inspection by hiding the drive core's calibration ring in the composting beds. The beat is defiant joy — the found family protecting itself — with Ulyana complicit and terrified.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Voss, suspecting the sabotage, threatens to seize the Verdance outright; the Compact fleet responds by moving weapons hot. Ulyana maintains the beacon's false certification publicly while privately mapping how to broadcast the truth. The beat is the lie straining under its own weight.

chapters.title: The Garden Under Guns
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Sef POVs. A Combine boarding action breaches the habitat; the children shelter in the seed vaults while Ulyana stalls the boarding officer with bureaucratic theater. The beat is fear transmuted into fierce protectiveness — the garden becomes a fortress of seedlings and children.

chapters.title: Sef's Confession
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, addressed to Ulyana. Sef reveals the full truth: the Meridian's aging-back was the beacon's original purpose — a test of whether the jump windows could reverse time's toll, and the mentor falsified records to hide that the experiment was declared a failure. The beat is devastating clarity: the beacon was never meant to protect anyone.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Two Choices
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With nine days left, Ulyana holds two options: recertify the beacon for either fleet and choose who survives the window, or broadcast the truth and risk both fleets firing rather than yielding. The beat is the loyalty-versus-truth dilemma at full pressure, with the children's faces behind every calculation.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Seed Vault
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, anchored in Sef. Ulyana tells the children everything and lets them vote on what he should do. Sef argues for the truth; the youngest argue for whichever choice keeps the garden. The beat is found family at its truest — trust given without guarantees.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Three days before window close, Ulyana transmits the mentor's sealed logs, the falsification, and the Meridian's experiment records to both fleets simultaneously — the truth as his final act of maintenance. The beat is terrifying release: the lie dies and everything it held up shakes.

chapters.title: What the Fleets Did
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Sef POVs as both fleets waver, then converge — not on each other, but on the Verdance, demanding the children and the drive core. The beat is the climax igniting: every gun pointed at one small garden, and Ulyana standing on its threshold.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Sef alternating POV, minute by minute. Ulyana proposes the unthinkable: the Meridian jumps with both fleets' representatives and the children aboard, sharing the window — the beacon's arbitration lock, repurposed, certifies a joint claim. The fleets, out of time and options, accept. The beat is the climax resolving through the very lie's machinery turned honest.

chapters.title: After the Jump
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The joint jump succeeds; the children age forward erratically but survive, and Sef wakes with a body nearly his true age and memories whole. The fleets, bound by shared survival, negotiate a provisional accord. The beat is exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Born
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, coda. Months later, the Verdance opens as a school and settlement; the beacon is decommissioned into a memorial that tells the truth, including the mentor's. Ulyana plants the last bed with the children and finally tends a garden for people who exist. The beat is inheritance redeemed — loyalty and truth reconciled in soil.
